title: security: restrict RAG logs and purge operations to trusted callers
body:
## Finding

Fixes exactly one Codex Security finding: **RAG log RLS allows anonymous read/write and log purging**.

Actual base SHA: `93525b3e522dfd97883e96027dcf41f301e0f7fd`
Head SHA at PR creation: `8fc665a7a45b36bb141c8dc6fabd4b8e03de7669`

Out of scope: user-profile credential/reset/verification disclosure, recommendation_feedback compatibility, other legacy Supabase Advisor findings, RAG retrieval/ranking/embedding/prompt/UI changes.

## Legacy tree and canonical Supabase tree

The current `database/migrations/` tree contains only `README_DEPRECATED.md`; the three legacy files were removed by commit `67c330a7b72f38e52a27374741929e766112fd67`. Their historical contents were audited at commit `2aac4502d11e2c10bbf3fc5e2aa920c839e15738`:

- `database/migrations/007_rag_observability.sql`
- `database/migrations/008_rag_log_retention.sql`
- `database/migrations/009_rag_log_add_fields.sql`

The active clean-replay contract is the canonical tree:

- `supabase/migrations/20260118090800_007_rag_observability.sql`
- `supabase/migrations/20260118090900_008_rag_log_retention.sql`
- `supabase/migrations/20260118091000_009_rag_log_add_fields.sql`

No historical migration was modified. The fix is forward-only in `20260712210000_restrict_rag_log_rls_and_purge_operations.sql`.

## Effective table / policy / ACL before and after

Before, from a complete canonical replay at the base SHA (historical 008 skipped only because the required CI image has no pg_cron):

- owner: `postgres`
- columns: `id, created_at, user_id, query_text, subject_code, paper_code, topic_id, mode, match_count, duration_ms, top_score, top_chunk_id, items, degraded, retries`
- important defaults preserved: UUID id, `created_at=now()`, `degraded=false`, `retries=0`
- indexes preserved: primary key, `idx_rag_search_logs_created_at`, `idx_rag_search_logs_subject`
- RLS: enabled
- FORCE RLS: enabled by the later repository-wide hardening migration
- table ACL: `authenticated=SELECT,INSERT`
- column ACL: no explicit `pg_attribute.attacl`, but table grants were effective across all columns
- policies: `insert_own_logs` and `select_own_logs`, both `TO PUBLIC`
- allow predicates: `auth.uid() IS NULL OR ...`

After:

- owner remains `postgres`
- columns/defaults/indexes are unchanged
- RLS and FORCE RLS are enabled
- every policy on `public.rag_search_logs` is removed
- PUBLIC, anon, authenticated, and service_role have no table privilege
- all current column ACLs are dynamically revoked from those four principals
- only the database owner retains table privileges

## Sensitive log fields

The protected row includes identity, raw query, scope, performance, result, and retry data: `user_id`, `query_text`, `subject_code`, `paper_code`, `topic_id`, `mode`, `match_count`, `duration_ms`, `top_score`, `top_chunk_id`, `items`, `degraded`, and `retries`.

## Caller inventory and database identities

| Surface | Database identity | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Browser `src/api/ragApi.js` | authenticated JWT request to server route | No direct table/RPC access; sends no log user id |
| `/api/rag/ask`, `/api/rag/search` | verified server auth context; retrieval client is service_role | No `rag_search_logs` / `rag_log_search` / purge call |
| Current telemetry recorder/sink | server process filesystem | JSONL/noop best-effort sink; no legacy table access |
| RAG benchmark/eval scripts | service-role retrieval client or mocks | No legacy table/RPC access |
| PostgreSQL migration/operations | postgres/database owner | Owns canonical maintenance compatibility |
| Historical pg_cron path | job username/creator role | Historical command is `SELECT public.rag_search_logs_purge(90);`; no job is produced by clean replay because the migration checks `cron_schedule` while pg_cron exposes `cron.schedule` |
| Tests | mock clients / SET ROLE principals | No external provider or remote Supabase |

Repository-wide exact-name searches found no current `.from('rag_search_logs')`, `.rpc('rag_log_search')`, or `.rpc('rag_search_logs_purge')` runtime caller.

## Browser direct-access audit

There is no legitimate browser direct logging or log-reading requirement. Browser code calls authenticated server RAG routes only. The migration-order/runtime contract scans the entire browser source tree and rejects future references to the table or either function.

## rag_log_search overload/signature audit

History contained:

1. 11 arguments in canonical 007.
2. 13 arguments in canonical 009, adding `in_degraded BOOLEAN` and `in_retries INTEGER`; 009 drops the 11-argument signature.

Pre-fix final catalog: one 13-argument overload, owner `postgres`, SECURITY DEFINER, mutable/default search_path, authenticated EXECUTE.

Post-fix: the same 13-argument argument/return contract, SECURITY INVOKER, `search_path=''`, schema-qualified table, and no PUBLIC/anon/authenticated/service_role EXECUTE. A dynamic `pg_proc` sweep revokes all four principals from every same-name overload.

No service_role grant is restored because the caller audit found no real checked-in caller. A future trusted caller requires a separate least-privilege migration and tests.

## Purge function and cron caller audit

Historical `rag_search_logs_purge(integer DEFAULT 90)` was SECURITY DEFINER, had no fixed search_path or validation, and default-created PUBLIC EXECUTE. A pg_cron-enabled isolated Supabase Postgres replay confirmed the function was executable by PUBLIC/anon/authenticated/service_role.

That replay also confirmed the historical `IF proname='cron_schedule'` check does not match pg_cron's real `cron.schedule` functions, so clean replay schedules no job. This does **not** prove production lacks a manually/existing job; no remote catalog was queried.

Post-fix purge is SECURITY INVOKER with empty search_path, schema-qualified table and pg_catalog helpers, owner-only execution, and the unchanged canonical `keep_days INTEGER DEFAULT 90` signature. Existing owner-created cron SQL calling `purge(90)` remains compatible. This migration does not create, delete, rename, or reschedule a production job.

## Parameter-validation design

`keep_days` must be non-NULL and between 1 and 3650 inclusive. Invalid inputs raise SQLSTATE `22023`. The deletion predicate remains strictly older than the calculated threshold.

## Server confused-deputy analysis

- Direct ask/search routes require the #1533 JWT boundary before RAG or telemetry work.
- Verified identity is stored on `req.auth_user_id` / `req.auth_user`.
- Ask now explicitly strips both `body.user_id` and `body.userId`; search already builds a canonical allowlisted input object.
- Query-string user identity is ignored.
- There is no service-role legacy log RPC forwarding path, so callers cannot currently substitute `in_user_id`.
- Current telemetry does not persist raw query text or result items to this table; it hashes normalized queries.
- Telemetry sink failure remains fail-open for the user request per the existing product contract, returns explicit `null`, and emits a redacted warning rather than a false recorded status.

## Service-role least-privilege matrix

| Capability | PUBLIC | anon | authenticated | service_role | postgres/owner |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| table SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE | no | no | no | no | owner privileges |
| canonical `rag_log_search` EXECUTE | no | no | no | no | yes |
| noncanonical logger overload EXECUTE | no | no | no | no | owner only |
| purge EXECUTE | no | no | no | no | yes |
| retention deletion | no | no | no | no | owner/owner-created cron |

## Migration strategy

The forward-only remediation:

- enables and forces RLS;
- drops all existing table policies;
- revokes table and column privileges from PUBLIC/anon/authenticated/service_role;
- replaces the canonical logger and purge with SECURITY INVOKER + empty search_path;
- preserves columns, defaults, indexes, 13-argument logger compatibility, degraded/retries, and the 90-day purge default;
- dynamically revokes every logger and purge overload;
- does not change cron scheduling.

## Final-catalog test design

`tests/evidence-ledger/rag-log-rls-security.sql` first asserts the real final replay catalog before any remediation reapplication: owner, exact columns/defaults, RLS/FORCE RLS, table/column ACLs, zero policies, logger/purge signatures, invoker mode, empty search_path, defaults, all overload ACLs, and conditional cron-owner compatibility.

It then uses transactional `SET ROLE anon/authenticated/service_role` behavior checks and owner fixtures. All fixtures roll back.

## Purge boundary tests

The SQL test proves:

- `purge(90)` deletes a 100-day row and preserves 2-day/12-hour rows.
- `purge(1)` deletes the 2-day row and preserves the 12-hour row.
- 0, negative, NULL, and 3651 are rejected with SQLSTATE 22023.
- canonical log fields/return behavior remain compatible for owner operations.

## Overload-sweep test

A separate transaction creates default-PUBLIC synthetic overloads for both function names, proves PUBLIC-derived anon/authenticated/service_role execution before remediation, replays the remediation, proves all four principals lose EXECUTE, confirms no canonical service_role grant appears, and rolls back.

## Exact local results

Passed:

- RAG log static contract: 1 suite / 6 tests.
- Final catalog + SET ROLE + purge + overload SQL: passed on exact clean replay.
- Complete canonical migration replay: passed in a brand-new `pgvector/pgvector:pg16` database; only historical 008 skipped under the repository-approved missing-pg_cron rule; the forward migration created the hardened purge.
- RAG direct-route/security/telemetry, API Route Integration, Security Baseline/Depth, and RAG Boundary Jest selection: 13 suites / 107 tests.
- Existing security migration-order contracts + Supabase audit-core tests: 8 suites / 146 tests.
- All seven PostgreSQL security DB contract files: passed (recommendation contract rerun with its required remediation-body fixture).
- API Route Integration summary: `status=pass`.
- Security Baseline report: `status=pass`.
- Security Depth summary: `status=pass`, no failures.
- RAG Boundary contract summary: `all_green=true`.
- Shared Rate Limit summary: `status=pass`.
- Repository audit-core against the final local catalog: no target RAG log/RPC/purge finding after the invoker change.
- ESLint on changed JavaScript: passed.
- `db-contract-gate.yml` YAML parse: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- final post-push Codex preflight: `top_status=healthy`; clean worktree; upstream ahead=0/behind=0.

Limitations observed accurately:

- `python3 scripts/phase2/check_db_contract.py` and `run_migration_smoke.py` executed but reported `status=skipped` because local psycopg/psycopg2 packages are absent. The GitHub job installs them.
- Supabase CLI 2.109.1 `db advisors --db-url` and `db lint --db-url` could not connect to the same disposable DB that `psql` could reach, returning `LegacyDbConnectError`.
- A pinned CLI 2.81.3 fallback could not finish downloading its native binary in this environment.
- `plpgsql_check` availability in `pgvector/pgvector:pg16` is 0, so DB lint is not claimed as passed.

## GitHub Actions status

All 22 check runs are terminal.

- Success (21): API Route Integration; Backend Consistency; Backend/platform ESLint; Boundary Contract (RAG Boundary Gate); Boundary Contract (RAG Boundary Tests); Boundary DB Guardrail; DB Contract + Migration Smoke; ESLint; Evidence Context RPC Security Contract; Mark Decision RPC Security Contract; PR Workflow Trust Boundary; RAG Log RLS Security Contract; Recommendation RLS Security Contract; Rubric Extraction RLS Security Contract; S1 Contract Gate; S2 Release Governance (Required); Security Baseline; Security Depth Gate; Security and Study Views Contract; Shared Rate Limit Gate; User Profile Role Security Contract.
- Skipped (1, intentional trusted-only path): Trusted Repository Workflow Trust Boundary.
- Failure/cancelled/timed_out/action_required: 0.

## Review thread status

Final review surfaces:

- Review submissions: 1 `COMMENTED` by `gemini-code-assist[bot]`; summary explicitly states there are no review comments/findings.
- Top-level PR conversation comments: 0.
- Inline review comments: 0.
- Review threads: 0 total, 0 unresolved, 0 outdated.
- Actionable review findings: 0.

## Remaining limitations

- No production, staging, linked, or remote Supabase connection was made.
- No remote logs were read/changed and no purge was run remotely.
- Production cron catalog state remains intentionally unverified; compatibility is based on the checked-in 90-day command and owner model.
- The migration has not been deployed.
- This PR is draft and must not be merged by the worker.

## Safety declarations

- **No remote Supabase was connected.**
- **No `supabase db push` was run.**
- **No real logs were deleted.**
- **No real embedding/LLM/provider was called.**
- **This migration is not deployed.**
- **Do not merge this draft PR from the worker flow.**

## Merge-blocker follow-up (2026-07-13)

Commit: `af22b8574b85c237317d24e24664ac9dd3670c57`

- Added explicit `BEGIN;` / `COMMIT;` around the complete forward-only remediation. The static contract asserts the first and last top-level statements and rejects transaction-breaking statements.
- Replaced the zero-iteration-only later-migration check with `laterMigrationIssues({ name, sql })` and 21 focused future-migration mutations/controls.
- Default-PUBLIC `rag_log_search(text)` and `rag_search_logs_purge(text)` overload mutations are rejected unless the final same-name definition is followed by a same-statement `pg_proc` all-overload revoke sweep covering PUBLIC, anon, authenticated, and service_role.
- Canonical safe redefinition without a post-definition sweep is rejected. Unsafe grants, blanket grants, target policies, RLS weakening, mutable search_path, SECURITY DEFINER, and unqualified sensitive relations are rejected.
- An unrelated owner-scoped policy and audited unrelated function remain accepted as the negative control.
- The overload SQL harness now receives the exact remediation body with only the statically asserted outer transaction statements removed, preserving its independent test transaction and final ROLLBACK. Post-test catalog verification found zero synthetic overloads.

Local follow-up results:

- Target static/mutation contract: 1 suite, 28/28 tests passed.
- All seven static security contracts: 7 suites, 161/161 tests passed.
- Brand-new pgvector/pg16 clean replay: 97 migrations applied; historical 008 skipped only under the existing missing-pg_cron rule.
- Final catalog / SET ROLE / purge / synthetic overload SQL: passed; both phases rolled back cleanly.
- All seven PostgreSQL security DB contracts: passed.
- RAG direct-route and telemetry: 4 suites, 24/24 tests passed.
- API route and security suites: 4 suites, 19/19 tests passed.
- API Route Integration: pass; Security Baseline: pass; Security Depth: pass with no failures; RAG Boundary: all_green=true; Shared Rate Limit: pass.
- ESLint, workflow YAML parse, and git diff --check: passed.
- Local Python DB contract/migration-smoke scripts executed but remained skipped because psycopg/psycopg2 are absent; the GitHub job installs these dependencies.

The PR remains draft. No remote Supabase connection, db push, remote purge, real log mutation, merge, or other finding was included.

### Follow-up GitHub terminal state

For head `af22b8574b85c237317d24e24664ac9dd3670c57`, all 22 checks are terminal: 21 success, 1 intentional trusted-only skip, 0 failures/cancellations/timeouts. Review state remains 1 non-actionable `COMMENTED` submission, 0 top-level comments, 0 inline comments, and 0 review threads (0 unresolved, 0 outdated).
